findings.summary: Signup gate is read before the work and recorded only after it, allowing concurrent requests to bypass the per-address ceiling.
findings.scenario: A script opens N connections at once, each reading a count of zero before any writes occur, thus passing the `blocked` check while the counter remains 0. This results in creating ~N accounts per window instead of adhering to the `perSignupIp` limit.

summary: The signup gate is read before the work and recorded only after it, allowing concurrent requests to bypass the per-address ceiling. This can lead to a large number of accounts being created in a short period, potentially overwhelming the system or violating rate limiting policies. · One high-severity issue found in the `reserve` function of `attemptLimiter.js`. The function does not handle concurrent requests correctly when a key is at its maximum count, leading to potential race conditions and violation of rate limits. · The signup gate is read before the work and recorded only after it, allowing multiple simultaneous signups to bypass the per-address ceiling. · The signup gate is read before the work and recorded only after it, allowing concurrent requests to bypass the per-address ceiling.
